summary: P95/P99 latency spikes and request timeouts correlated with continuous-batching behavior
description:
Issue summary:
Production customer (FastRetail Inc.) reports P95/P99 latency spikes and intermittent 504 timeouts for text-generation API over the last 48 hours. Spikes coincide with high short-lived burst traffic patterns.

Impact:
- Intermittent user-facing timeouts impacting checkout personalization flows for ~8% of requests during peak bursts.
- Elevated p95/p99 from baseline ~350ms to bursts >2.5s; p50 largely unaffected.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) customer in us-east region.
- Serving runtime version: v3.14.2
- Scheduler version: v2.8.1
- Observed on models: rwk-v1-13B and gpt-mini-16k.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer runs many short requests (~8-40 tokens) with high concurrency and frequent, irregular bursts.
2) Continuous-batching logic accumulates requests into a single batch to improve throughput.
3) During bursts, batch sizes oscillate rapidly; some requests wait for batch completion leading to long tail latency.
4) When backend experiences transient slow kernels (GPU context switch/eviction), waiting requests see timeouts.

Observed behavior / Evidence:
- Grafana dashboard: "serving/p99_latency_by_model" spikes aligning with burst timestamps (links in comments).
- Traces show requests spending extra time in "batch_queue_wait" before entering inference.
- Backend logs contain repeated kernel warmup messages and occasional gRPC retry logs.
- Support throttles/quotas not hit; CPU/GPU utilization moderate, but queue depths high.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous batching should increase throughput without causing request-level p99 regressions; tail should remain bounded through adaptive batching heuristics.

Initial hypothesis:
- Adaptive continuous-batcher heuristic overly aggressive: waits to form larger batches during short bursts (to maximize throughput) even when waiting increases tail latency for latency-sensitive requests.
- Scheduler may be placing some requests on GPU worker with transient slowdown (noisy neighbor or kernel warmup).

Workaround implemented:
- Applied per-customer routing override to reduce batch windows and prefer smaller, latency-optimized batches for FastRetail (feature flag: routing.batch_profile=latency).
- Increased request-level timeout temporarily from 3s to 6s for in-flight requests to reduce user errors while investigation continues.
comments: 2026-02-20 | Support - Aisha Khan: Initial ticket created after customer reported spikes. Captured preliminary graphs from FastRetail and asked for request IDs and example traces. Added SRE and serving-runtime oncall.

2026-02-20 | SRE - Marco Rivera: Looked at infra metrics. Noted elevated batch_queue_depth correlated with spikes. No GPU OOMs; occasional context-switch messages. Added hypothesis about adaptive batching waiting too long during bursty traffic.

2026-02-21 | Eng - Priya Shah (serving-runtime): Reproduced with local load generator using bursty short requests. Instrumentation shows batch_wait_time percentile grows with burst frequency. Opening PR to add dynamic max-wait fallback for latency profiles. See PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/789.

2026-02-21 | Support - Aisha Khan: Notified customer of investigation and applied routing override to reduce batch window. Customer confirmed immediate p95 improvement on their next test run (reduced failures).

2026-02-22 | Eng - Diego Martinez: Deployed canary of change lowering max_batch_wait for latency-profile; canary in us-east for dedicated hosts. Initial telemetry shows p99 down ~40% for small-token requests on canary hosts. Continuing expansion and monitoring.

2026-02-23 | SRE - Marco Rivera: Observed one instance of slowed GPU worker (driver jitter) causing a backlog. Marked host for maintenance and applied node drain to prevent future evictions during peak. Added host to follow-up list.
2026-02-24 | Support - Aisha Khan: Customer reports significant improvement after routing override and platform canary. Will keep ticket open until full rollout and postmortem complete.
follow_up_actions: Roll out adaptive max_batch_wait change to all serving clusters (ENG-PR 789)
Add a latency-profile knob to customer routing with documentation
Investigate scheduler placement to avoid noisy GPU hosts; add auto-drain on driver jitter detection
Draft postmortem and update continuous-batching runbook with detection/mitigation steps
